findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R2/probe_concurrent.py: run 1 stops WAITING_FOR_MODEL (quota). `git branch --track other-session-work origin/canon` in the same repo (adds [branch "other-session-work"] to .git/config). Run 2 -> BLOCKED, blocker kind TAMPER, reason 'GIT_CONTROL: git_control changed since the plan'. git push -u and git switch -c <x> origin/<y> write config the same way. Fails closed (no false ACCEPT), but the doc says other sessions legitimately move other branches, and regular owner unblocks dilute TAMPER as a signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Digest only the execution- and interpretation-relevant config (core.*, filter.*, diff.*, merge.*, include/includeIf, extensions.*, alias.*, protocol/transport settings), or exclude branch.<name>.* and remote.*.fetch for branches other than the milestone's; document which config changes are treated as tampering.
findings.title: PLAN-anchored GIT_CONTROL digest hashes the whole shared .git/config, so routine branch/tracking writes by other sessions block the milestone as TAMPER

findings.evidence: write_json now returns sha256 of the str written via Path.write_text, and reviewer_stdout.txt / reviewer_result.txt are written with write_text and hashed from the in-memory str. verify and accepted_review hash read_bytes(). On Windows write_text translates \n to \r\n, so round_sha256, stdout_sha256 and result_sha256 never match: every run blocks TAMPER and no milestone can reach VERIFIED. Windows is out of scope in the plan section 4, but the lifecycle doc says 'On the owner's PC the same checks apply'. Code reasoning only; not run on Windows.
findings.suggested_fix: Write all hashed files with newline='' (or write_bytes of the encoded str) so the hashed bytes and the stored bytes are identical.
findings.title: Hashes compare text-mode writes with bytes read back: on Windows every round fails verify (fails closed)
